title: Reserved capacity staleness pruning and rollback procedure
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: We have observed a small but recurring class of billing/availability anomalies where reserved capacity leases (monthly/daily windows) become stale after multi-step failures (leader failover + consumer clock skew + partial write). Stale leases lead to: 1) tenants seeing sudden dropped reserved throughput when a reaper prunes a lease aggressively; 2) occasional double-counting during ‘soft rollback’ compensations; 3) accounting mismatches requiring manual billing credits. This ticket designs a deterministic pruning + rollback flow that is idempotent, latency-safe, and reconciles accounting cleanly for reserved pools.
background: Current system uses a per-tenant lease ledger with epoch anchored resets. During leader failover we might replay partial lease updates. There is also a background reaper that prunes leases older than X hours; that process can remove a still-valid but temporarily disconnected tenant reservation. Past incidents (link in related_links) show errors arise when pruning occurs between a delayed usage write and the ledger checkpoint. We need a formalized, testable procedure to: detect staleness confidently, gracefully prune orphaned reservations, and run compensating transactions to correct billing without customer-visible disruptions.
goals: Define deterministic staleness detection using multi-sourced heartbeats and ledger watermarks
Implement a tenant-level grace/lease extension mechanism to avoid premature pruning
Create an idempotent rollback/compensation procedure for usage accounting and billing reconciliation
Provide telemetry, alerts, and a safe canary rollout to limit customer impact
non_goals: Rewrite the entire quota engine (this is an incremental mitigation)
Address unrelated rate-limiter fairness improvements (separate project)
proposal_summary: Add a two-step staleness verification before pruning: (A) confirm ledger write-age > threshold AND (B) validate absence of recent tenant heartbeat or activity from routing proxies. If both hold, mark the lease as 'candidate-prune' and move it into a hold state for configurable hold_duration (default 10m) during which we attempt a lease refresh RPC to the tenant control-plane. If refresh fails, we execute an idempotent prune and emit a reconcile token to the billing pipeline. If prune is later found to remove an active reservation, we support a compensating transaction path that replays usage deltas, applies a pro-rated credit, and writes an audit entry. All operations are idempotent via per-lease reconcile-token and monotonic sequence numbers.
implementation_steps: DB: add 'candidate_prune' flag and last_heartbeat_at, reconcile_token (string) columns to reservation table (backfill for existing rows) - migration guarded behind feature flag
API: expose tenant heartbeat endpoint (lightweight) from reserved agent; routing proxies will forward heartbeats detected on active connections
Reaper change: replace hard prune with candidate->hold->prune state machine and attempt refresh RPC; use exponential backoff for refresh attempts
Accounting: emit reconcile_token with any prune event to billing Kafka topic; billing consumer will treat reconcile_token as an idempotency key
Compensating flow: implement a 'replay-usage' job that accepts reconcile_token and applies deltas or credits depending on reconciliation outcome
Telemetry: add metrics and dashboards for candidate_prune_count, prune_failures, reconcile_token_emit_rate, compensating_tx_rate
Runbook: document operator steps for a failed reconcile (how to surface ledger rows, manually re-run replay-usage, and issue customer credits)
Tests: unit tests for state machine, integration tests simulating failovers and clock skew, chaos test that kills leader during prune window
Rollout: enable feature flag in staging; canary to 5% of tenants (non-enterprise); monitor for 72h before wider rollout
acceptance_criteria: No increase in 5xx errors for reserved API during canary period
Candidate_prune -> prune transitions only after hold_duration and failed refresh RPC
All prune events emit reconcile_token and billing consumer successfully idempotent-processes tokens in staging
Compensating replay can correct historical usage for at least 3 test incidents simulated in integration test
Dashboards show clear counts and a pinned alert if prune_rate > baseline * 2
testing_plan: Unit tests for database migration idempotency and no-op backfills
Integration test harness that simulates the sequence: leader failover -> delayed usage write -> reaper run; verify prune path and compensating replay
Chaos test: intermittent network partitions between router and control plane and ensure heartbeat resilience
Load test: ensure reaper hold state does not create unbounded memory growth under heavy tenant churn
Billing simulation: run billing consumer against a recorded prune event stream to validate idempotency and credit correctness
telemetry: logs: structured audit entries with reconcile_token, lease_id, attempted_by, timestamp
traces: reaper->refreshRPC->prune spans with tags to identify tenant and region
rollback_plan: Feature flag off: immediately stop new candidate_prune transitions (legacy reaper remains disabled until fallback tested)
Idempotent compensating job: if a prune caused a customer-visible regressed capacity, run replay-usage with reconcile_token to restore usage lines and apply a pro-rated credit
Database rollback: migration is additive (new columns) and guarded; if migration causes unexpected load, throttle migrations using per-shard backfill window
Emergency manual: operators can flip 'prevent_prune' for a tenant row to avoid automated prune while debugging
operational_considerations: Clock skew: system must use monotonic server timestamps for critical comparisons; Do not rely solely on client-reported times
Backpressure: avoid blocking reaper work queue during mass-purge; process in bounded concurrency batches
Data retention: reconcile_token audit entries kept for 90 days to allow billing queries and customer dispute resolution
Security: reconcile_token must be opaque UUIDs; no PII carried in tokens
Performance: hold_duration default tuned to 10m to balance false positives vs memory usage
